title: 5 diet tips for hardgainers
summary: NH gives five diet tips for skinny guys who struggle to gain weight: reframe 'hardgainer' as a dietary instruction rather than a curse, eat more frequent meals, base the diet on whole foods but fill the gap with palatable calorie-dense foods, drink homemade calorie shakes, and gain slowly over years rather than force-feeding.

claims.claim: A true hardgainer is someone whose hormonal profile makes lean mass hard to gain; needing a lot of calories doesn't make you one.
No young male is incapable of gaining weight; if you ate enough to exceed TDEE you would gain. The issue is a high metabolism or appetite mismatch.
Easy gainers should focus more on training since they gain regardless; hardgainers should focus more effort on eating enough to feed their workouts.
Easy gainers aren't simply advantaged: they need fewer calories and often have bigger appetites, so getting shredded is harder for them.
Treat the hardgainer label as an indication of what to do, not a curse; you just need to be extra diligent with diet.
Hardgainers often have weak appetites that shut off within five or six minutes of a meal.
Don't shovel food down quickly; chew properly for digestion and nutrient absorption.
Six meals a day is a myth for bodybuilders in general but useful for hardgainers: splitting meals lets the stomach empty repeatedly so you can fit in the calories.
The worst thing a hardgainer can do is eat only once or twice a day; schedule dedicated meal times.
He has a slow metabolism and mild appetite and can sometimes eat one meal a day and maintain 210 lb.
Whole foods fill you up fast, making a pure clean bulk hard for hardgainers; don't do a pure dirty bulk either.
Base the bulk mostly on whole foods, then top up with palatable calorie-dense foods you enjoy once macros and micros are met.
Bad foods exist: foods whose only benefit is calories, like cake (fat and sugar, no vitamins or minerals); they're empty calories but won't kill you in a big surplus.
Too many tall skinny guys follow bro diets of chicken and broccoli and don't grow because they don't eat enough; eat the cake or pizza, but balance it for health (sugar, sodium).
Commercial weight gainers are garbage: pure sugar, industrial by-products, and expensive.

Drink your calories with homemade blender shakes (peanut butter, milks, avocado, blueberries) to get hundreds of calories easily, sipped through the day or as a big bottle before bed; watch that raw eggs don't spoil.
He is not a fan of GOMAD: the weight gain and potential health consequences aren't worth it, with too much milk fat and more protein than the body can use.
Take your time: novice programs expect fast strength gains, but skinny young males take years to reach those numbers; don't rush.
Muscle gain slows over time and is bounded by your years with a prime hormonal profile, so rushing to a bodyweight just to stall for years is pointless.
Even a tall 6'5 natural won't be 300 lb ripped; do a slow weight gain.
Force-feeding leads to nausea and failure; small daily surpluses beat occasional 3,000 kcal surplus days, just as a 2,000 kcal cheat meal wrecks a 200 kcal daily deficit.
He started at 110 lb and gained 100 lb over 10 years; people who gain 100 lb in three years usually don't build the same quality of muscle.
Gaining slowly teaches the body to turn food into muscle; flooding it with surplus just stores fat and may worsen fat distribution.
Ignore YouTube fitness strength standards; gaining muscle and some fat together gives a bulkier, more aesthetic look.
If you stay skinny, you aren't eating enough.
Hardgainers may do better with shorter workouts because they lack work capacity; focus mainly on diet first, and training becomes the priority once the body is bigger.
